title: Picks
summary: Agents ask the owner for human judgments in T3 Code itself. A new MCP tool, request_picks, takes a batch of 1-200 questions, each with 2-4 image or video options (absolute paths, copied into the attachments store) and an optional exact display box; it returns pending at once. The server shuffles each question's options and the Picks inbox (a sidebar item with the open count, and a /picks page across connected environments) shows them by place only, one question at a time, with keys 1-4, 0 for can't tell, N for a note and arrows. Each answer is saved as it is made; Done records the batch answered and wakes the asking thread with one message listing every answer unblinded, plus the same as JSON. Batches are a pick_request turn item on the asking thread, closed without a wake when the thread is stopped, settled, archived or deleted. The open-batch partial index is created idempotently at startup rather than as a numbered migration, so the patch never collides with upstream's migration ids.

journeys.proves: A fixture ACP agent calls request_picks on the built app's real /mcp endpoint with its thread's credential; the sidebar shows 1 waiting; the owner opens the batch in the Picks inbox, answers with 2, 0 (can't tell), N plus a note and 1, and presses Done; the asking thread shows the answered card and the wake, and the agent replies with every answer unblinded from the wake's JSON.
